messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Female workers with serum vitamin D below 10 ng/mL had higher odds of depressive symptoms (CES-D 16 or above) than those with higher levels.
Sentence: "The odds ratio of the depressive symptom group with a CES-D score of 16 or above being in the deficiency group with a serum vitamin D level less than 10 ng/mL was found to be 1.55 (95 % CI = 1.15-2.07)."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (CES-D score of 16 or above)
Population: 1054 Korean female workers in the manufacturing industry undergoing physical examinations
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (deficiency below 10 ng/mL), measured, not given
Comparator: Serum vitamin D 10 ng/mL or higher
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 1,054
baseline_vitamin_d_status: below_20_ng_ml

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: In the RCT, vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood, including depression.
Sentence: "The vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood and serum concentrations of BDNF."
Measured as: depression (mood status)
Population: Healthy subjects with inadequate serum vitamin C (<50 μmol/L), n = 46
Intervention: Vitamin C 500 mg twice a day for 4 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 260
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
